{"id": "107:2/q10", "question": "What historical incident is reported behind this description?", "turns_on": "The named person and the reported circumstances; the Abū Sufyān reports also vary on how many camels were slaughtered.", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q10/p1", "position": "An orphan sought food from Abū Sufyān after he slaughtered camels, and he struck the child with a stick.", "reasons": "Ibn Jurayj supplies the occasion; al-Wāḥidī says two camels each week, Abū Ḥayyān says a camel weekly, and other accounts mention a camel or weekly camels without the same number. These numerical variants remain explicit here."}, {"id": "107:2/q10/p2", "position": "An orphan under Abū Jahl's guardianship came unclothed seeking his own money, and he pushed the child away.", "reasons": "Bursevī adds that Quraysh sent the boy to Muḥammad in mockery; the Prophet accompanied him and Abū Jahl paid. Abū Jahl said he feared a spear by Muḥammad, answering an accusation that he had converted."}, {"id": "107:2/q10/p3", "position": "The opening about the judgment-denier and orphan-repeller was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī attributes this to Mujāhid and al-Kalbī, while Study Quran names Muqātil and al-Kalbī; Kur'an Yolu reports the occasion without incident details."}]}
{"id": "107:2/q11", "question": "What ethical significance does repelling the orphan have?", "turns_on": "These are complementary emphases: diagnosis of denial and the positive duty owed to vulnerable people.", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q11/p1", "position": "Cruelty to an orphan exposes denial of judgment or religion: faith and fear of reckoning should produce mercy and care.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī calls abuse an active vice and failure to urge food an omission, examples rather than a complete list; al-Biqāʿī says denial hardens the heart and makes outward signs reveal hidden disbelief, but Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr cautions that a Muslim may commit such acts without thereby necessarily being a denier. Quṭb says true assent prompts action, not merely verbal claim or ritual, and distinguishes God's measure from juristic status. Ṭabāṭabāʾī says fear of consequence would bring mercy. Corpus Coranicum links eschatological awareness and solidarity with 92:5–9 and its absence with 104:1–3. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ says social duty exceeds private worship; Kur'an Yolu calls these examples especially destructive Meccan conduct and Ibn ʿĀshūr's broad condemnation of cruelty."}, {"id": "107:2/q11/p2", "position": "It demands respect for the weak, protection of their rights, and practical solidarity.", "reasons": "Bint al-Shāṭiʾ surveys orphan pairings with poor, captive, traveler and enslaved people (76:8; 90:16; 93:6–8; 2:177; 4:36) and the orphan's social right (8:41; 59:7; 2:177,215,83; 4:36). Al-Qurṭubī reports a Prophetic promise of Paradise for one caring for a Muslim orphan until self-sufficiency, without grading. Iṣlāḥī cites 89:17, Abū Bakr's maxim that the weak are strongest until their rights arrive, and calls for upholding their cause. Kur'an Yolu urges organized charitable institutions; al-Biqāʿī cites a Prophetic supplication for love of the poor and says withholding kind words foretells withheld wealth. Al-Qushayrī quotes mercy being removed only from a wretched heart."}]}
{"id": "107:2/q12", "question": "How do the orphan and poor clauses work together?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q12/p1", "position": "The first names active injury and the second omission of encouragement; each implies the counterpart left unstated in the other.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī contrasts the active offense and omitted urging; al-Biqāʿī says the orphan's shove implies contempt in the second clause and the poor clause's urging implies encouragement owed in the first; both signal injury to the weak and neglected kindness."}]}
{"id": "107:2/q13", "question": "How does the passage relate orphan abuse to later prayer failings?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q13/p1", "position": "Social and devotional failings together reveal a failure of sincere faith, with the later warning intensifying the rebuke.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf says the first warning shows sin's link to weak certainty before woe to worshippers; al-Thaʿlabī transmits Qatāda on heedless prayer and Ibn ʿAbbās on hypocrites who pray publicly but not privately (4:142), plus a Prophetic warning about lacking hope of reward or fear when abandoning prayer. Al-Biqāʿī likens trait descriptions to reports about hypocrisy and fornication, and links 8:4's believers who pray and spend. Elmalılı calls religious pretenders more surprising than open deniers. {"id": "107:2/q14", "question": "How does this verse connect with other passages and nearby sūras?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q14/p1", "position": "It belongs to a recurring Qur'anic pattern of honoring orphans and feeding the needy, grounded in God's favors and final accountability.", "reasons": "Corpus Coranicum compares vice lists 89:17–18, virtue list 90:13–16, and 93:9; 69:34; 74:44, plus 83:1–4 and Biblical orphan/widow/poor pairings and Matthew 25's eschatological charity. It says 106's earlier favors complement this sūra's future accountability. Al-Biqāʿī compares arrogance with the elephant people (105:1) and the miser's illusion of immortal wealth (104:3). Elmalılı connects Quraysh (106), Humaza (104), and Kawthar's summing of earlier sūras, especially from 93. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ contrasts God's sheltering the orphan Prophet with the repeller. Study Quran links orphan inheritance passages."}]}
{"id": "107:2/q15", "question": "What inward meaning is drawn from the orphan's repulsion?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q15/p1", "position": "The predatory self overpowers the orphan-like heart and drives it from spiritual nourishment.", "reasons": "Bursevī explicitly reports this inward reading; al-Qāshānī describes the excessive predatory soul harming the weak orphan in the outward description."}]}

{"id": "107:2/q18", "question": "How does this Qur'anic phrase relate to poetry's meter?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "107:2/q18/p1", "position": "The opening can coincide with khafīf meter without making the Qur'an poetry.", "reasons": "Al-Burhān treats complete lines, multiple lines and hemistichs that happen to scan, and reports the al-Māʿūn opening as khafīf; Abū Nuwās recast the lines in khafīf and adjusted them to فذاك الذي in his poem."}]}

{"id": "107:4/q02", "question": "How is the threat of wayl understood?", "turns_on": "Whether wayl is explained as the punishment generally or as a particular valley in Hell.", "positions": [{"id": "107:4/q02/p1", "position": "It announces punishment or ruin for the condemned worshippers.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī calls it punishment; al-Burṣawī infers severe punishment from their treatment of the orphan and poor. {"id": "107:4/q03", "question": "What is the grammatical role of the lām in 'to the worshippers'?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "107:4/q03/p1", "position": "The prepositional phrase with lām is the predicate of fa-wayl.", "reasons": "Al-Samīn gives this parsing alongside the consequential force of fāʾ."}]}
{"id": "107:4/q04", "question": "Why does the verse say 'worshippers' instead of using a pronoun?", "turns_on": "Whether the description replaces a pronoun for the same denier, broadens a specific case, mocks nonpraying people, or defines a standing class liable to prayer.", "positions": [{"id": "107:4/q04/p1", "position": "The explicit descriptive noun exposes another vice of the same people and heightens the warning.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī's analysis makes their description replace a pronoun for the deniers, who also neglect prayer, show off and withhold alms. {"id": "107:4/q05", "question": "How can the plural worshippers relate grammatically to the earlier singular denier?", "turns_on": "The grammatical treatment of fa-dhālika, the omitted answer of araʾayta, and whether a generic singular can take a descriptive plural in place of a pronoun.", "positions": [{"id": "107:4/q05/p1", "position": "The earlier singular denotes a generic class and so can be resumed by the plural worshippers.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī joins fa-dhālika to the denier, omits araʾayta's answer as supplied by the following warning, and reads the descriptive plural for a pronoun. {"id": "107:4/q06", "question": "Who are the worshippers threatened here?", "turns_on": "Whether the latter verses address the earlier deniers or another group, when they were revealed, and whether their outward prayer is hypocritical Islamic prayer or an older distorted ritual.", "positions": [{"id": "107:4/q06/p1", "position": "They are hypocrites who pray publicly for show but neglect or abandon prayer in private.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās adds withholding borrowed household goods out of spite; al-Ḥasan says they expect no reward for timely prayer and fear no penalty for lateness, or feel no regret on missing it. {"id": "107:4/q14", "question": "Where and when was the sūra or this warning revealed?", "turns_on": "Whether ostentation and hypocritical prayer require a Medinan setting, or can describe an older Meccan ritual and a thematically unified sūra.", "positions": [{"id": "107:4/q14/p1", "position": "The whole sūra was revealed in Mecca.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī transmits Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima and Qatāda; Ibn ʿĀshūr reports a majority and gives a possible seventeenth place after al-Takāthur and before al-Kāfirūn.
